title: File Text Replacement (partial)
domain: In-memory STRING! text only; no file read/write capability is available in the pinned native Glon CLI.
description: Partial implementation of the REBOL 2 Cookbook file text replacement program. The in-memory first-occurrence replacement is implemented in Glon; the file read/write round trip is blocked by missing host I/O.
attribution: Original REBOL 2 Cookbook recipe 'Replace Text in a File' by Carl Sassenrath (archived recipe linked in the reference source pane). The partial Glon implementation is original for this challenge.
reference: REBOL replace changes only the first occurrence of the target string and leaves later occurrences unchanged. The six cases below test beginning, middle, end, no match, multiple matches and empty text.
blocker: Complete file operation cannot be reproduced with the pinned native `glon` CLI and published vocabulary. The CLI has no file read/write words; the WASM host has no filesystem; the desktop GLON_LIVE proof exposes an asynchronous fs-read request/reply but no general Glon file-write binding. No host-side replacement or file processing is substituted.
host_dependency: None available for complete operation. A future complete challenge would require documented Glon file read and write capabilities.

cases.reference: Only the first of several occurrences changes.
Empty file text remains empty; s/print adds a newline.

known_limitations: Only the in-memory string replacement is implemented and tested. The original four-line REBOL program's file read/write round trip is not reproduced.
The pinned native glon CLI treats arguments as Glon source files and exposes no file I/O vocabulary.
The browser/WASM host has no filesystem. The desktop proof exposes fs-read but no general Glon file-write binding.
The partial implementation uses the published optional strings-ext library (s/slice) plus s/+, s/= and s/length. The vendored strings-ext.glon is an exact copy from the pinned upstream commit.
No C, Python, shell or host-side text replacement is used. No language or runtime extension was added.
An empty search pattern is outside this challenge's tested contract.

reference_implementation.title: Replace Text in a File — original REBOL 2 Cookbook program
reference_implementation.attribution: Author: Carl Sassenrath. REBOL Cookbook, recipe 0004, 'Replace Text in a File'.
reference_implementation.notes: Reads %doc.txt, replaces the first occurrence of "web" with "rebol", and writes the modified contents back to the same file.

layers.rebol: REBOL 2 provides its own runtime and series/file facilities. This comparison does not assert which of read, replace or write are core primitives in REBOL 2.
layers.glon: Frozen S1 has seven primitives and the R0 evaluator has no file or replace primitive. In-memory string operations are library code.
layers.note: Different substrate layers; no source-size comparison.

layers.rebol: replace is a mezzanine in Oldes' Rebol 3 at src/mezz/mezz-series.reb:129. This does not establish the exact implementation or provenance of REBOL 2's replace.
layers.glon: replace-first is a reusable Glon library implementation over s/slice, s/+, s/= and s/length. It implements first-occurrence replacement on in-memory strings only.
layers.note: The Glon listing is a library function, not an application equivalent.

layers.rebol: The Cookbook application reads a file, invokes the existing replace mezzanine, and writes the same file.
layers.glon: No complete application is implemented. File read/write is unavailable in the pinned native CLI; only an in-memory partial replacement job is tested.
layers.note: This is where the implementations differ: REBOL has file I/O; Glon does not.

implementation_comparison.notice: Source sizes are factual metadata labelled by abstraction layer. They do not compare equivalent implementation layers and are not a concision claim. REBOL's application listing uses existing read/replace/write facilities; Glon's listing is a reusable library function and its file application is incomplete.
